Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Quadratic Functions

Find the Peak: Completing the Square

Turning any jump equation into vertex form

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Completing the Square
Standards
HSA-SSE.B.3b, HSA-REI.B.4a, HSA-REI.B.4b

Students complete the square to rewrite quadratics in vertex form and to solve equations, and use it to find the peak of jumps given in standard form.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Complete the square for x2 + bx.
  • Rewrite y = ax2 + bx + c in vertex form.
  • Solve quadratic equations by completing the square.
  • Find a jump’s peak and landing from its standard-form equation.

3Essential question

If a jump’s equation hides its peak, how can algebra reveal it?

5MTB connection

Physics gives a jump’s path in standard form, because it comes from takeoff height, speed and gravity. Completing the square rewrites it in vertex form, revealing the peak without graphing.

That peak tells a builder how much clearance is needed above a gap or a deck.

The mathOn the trail
Standard formThe path from takeoff height and speed
Completing the squareFinding the peak by algebra
Vertex formPeak height and distance in the equation
SolvingWhere the rider lands

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Compare Three Jumps

Complete the square to find the peak and landing of three jumps, and choose the best design for a beginner line.

You’ll need: Calculator (for square roots); Graph paper or graphing app to check

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
